name: Network Information API and Save-Data
plain: Exposes estimated connection type, speed and data saver preference.
meaning: navigator.connection returns effectiveType (4g, 3g...), rtt rounded to 25 ms, downlink rounded to 25 kbps steps (max 10 Mbps) and saveData. Chrome on Android adds type (wifi, cellular); other browsers do not support it.

web.api: navigator.connection.effectiveType, rtt, downlink, saveData; Save-Data and Downlink request headers

limits.headline: Can see a rough guess of your connection type, speed and data saver setting
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads, or when your connection changes
can: Get a speed class such as 4g or 3g
Get rounded delay and download speed, with speed capped at 10 Mbps
Learn if Data Saver is on
On Chrome for Android, see if you use Wi-Fi or mobile data
cannot: Get exact speeds, since numbers are rounded
See your Wi-Fi name or password
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet support it. Safari and Firefox do not.

story.what_it_is: A page can see your estimated connection type and speed, and whether Data Saver is on.

marketing.name: Network Information API
marketing.pitch: Lets a page see the type of connection and adjust, such as sending less data on a slow one.

marketing.name: Save-Data
marketing.pitch: Google describes a hint that tells a site you want to use less data, so it can send lighter pages.

story.for_you: You get no prompt. A site may quietly send smaller images or lower quality video when you are on a slow connection or have Data Saver on. Pages feel faster and use less data.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to adapt quality to the network. Streaming and real time apps pick a safe level to avoid buffering. It is also a small signal for device ID and location hints.

use_cases.example: A streaming site starts at lower video quality on a slow connection, then raises it.
A cloud gaming page like Xbox Cloud Gaming or GeForce NOW picks stream quality based on your connection.
A video call site lowers video size when your network gets weak, to keep the voice clear.
A shop sends smaller product photos to people on Save Data or slow mobile.
A news site skips autoplay video for people who turned on Data Saver.
An ad network lowers ad size on slow networks to avoid slowing the page.
A fraud tool uses connection type as a small clue that does not match the claimed device.

technical_bounds: Estimates, not measurements of the real line

value.abuse: Adds up to 2 bits of network class; mobile vs wifi

history.change: Values rounded and capped to reduce fingerprinting
